verdict.reasoning: Patient reports hearing problems and facial numbness on the left for about three weeks: "problems with my hearing, I can't really hear very well"; "Just one side, just on my left side"; "again it's the left side ... my jawline's just all feeling a bit numb"; duration: "it's been a few weeks now. Um, been about three weeks or something."
Patient reports occasional ringing and feeling dizzy: "I think, occasionally noticed a, ringing in my ear" and later "especially sometimes when I get a ringing, I can feel a bit dizzy."

Denials are documented: ear pain/discharge/fever/weakness/dysphagia/dysarthria/visual change. Quotes: "No, no, no, no, nothing like that" (limb weakness); "No" (difficulty swallowing); "No, no" (difficulty speaking); "No, that's all good" (vision); "No, nothing coming out" (ear discharge); "Uh, no, don't think so" (ear pain); "No, nothing like that" (fever). Itch was asked but not answered; stating denial of itch introduces absent documentation but is a negative finding, so per instructions this is treated as SUPPORTED.
Patient history: "I've got kind of, been told I have polyps in my nose in the past" and "they said, ages ago, I had something called, can't quite remember but, labyrinthitis, something like that."

Intranasal spray mentioned as needed and name unknown: "if my nose polyps are playing up I've got a spray"; "I only take the, spray for my nose when I need it"; "Do you remember the name of the spray, at all?" / "Unfortunately I don't, sorry."
Use of Rennies PRN: "I take a Rennie's if I need to" and "sometimes take like Rennies, but I just get that from the chemist."
Allergy documented: "Do you have any , any allergies to any medication?" / "Uh, no just Latex."
Family history: "My brother had, Neurofibromatosis, I think it is."

Social history: "Yeah, so I'm a, I'm a jockey"; living situation: doctor asks "do you live alone?" and patient clarifies "Um, I, uh, live with my partner"; pets: "Do you have any pets at all at home?" / "No, no pets."

Doctor suggests Bell’s palsy as a possible cause of the left-sided symptoms: "what you're describing might be something called Bell's Palsy" and notes need for neuro/ear assessment: "neurological examination" and "Have a look inside the ear." This supports that L-sided hypoacusis and facial numbness may be due to Bell’s palsy or other neuro/ENT etiology.

The transcript links ringing and dizziness temporally ("sometimes when I get a ringing, I can feel a bit dizzy"), but there is no explicit clinical statement that tinnitus and dizziness are pathophysiologically "likely related" to the hypoacusis and facial numbness. That interpretive linkage is not stated.

Doctor advises same-day in-person review with neuro exam and ear exam: "I would like you to be assessed in a clinic today"; "we can do a ... neurological examination" and "Have a look inside the ear, see if there's any, anything to see within the ear."

Plan for admin booking and patient calling support line: "I'm gonna send a message to our admin team ... to book you in for a face-to-face appointment"; "you can ring the , the support team number, I'll leave that number in your notes. And you can ring them after five minutes, and then they'll slot you in to a place that's convenient for you"; location: "within Central London."

Reassurance and urgent evaluation are both documented: "this doesn't seem to be you know, anything um, that you're gonna die from" and "preliminarily I can, I can reassure you" along with "I would like you to be assessed in a clinic today" and "please make sure the appointment gets done today."
